title: Saul affirms that the Lord rewards one who spares his enemy
speaker: Saul
note: Casuistic maxim (‘If someone finds his enemy in distress…’) generalizing David’s mercy; compare Proverbs 25:21–22. Not covered by ot-1-samuel-v24-22.

title: Nabal’s servant urges Abigail to act before disaster strikes
speaker: one of Nabal’s young men
note: ‘Now know and see what you will do’ prompts Abigail’s intervention; a servant’s urging like the chapter’s other recorded requests.

title: Abigail asks David to hear her and disregard foolish Nabal
speaker: Abigail
note: Opening requests of Abigail’s plea; only 25:27 and 25:30–31 of her speech are recorded.

title: Abigail asks David to forgive her trespass
speaker: Abigail
note: ‘Please take away your handmaid’s lawless deed’ is a request to David, not a prayer; 25:29 is assurance and needs nothing.

title: David forbids Abishai to strike Saul and takes spear and flask
speaker: David
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Adds 26:10–11: David restates the prohibition and orders, ‘take the spear… and the water flask, and let us go.’

title: David asks Achish for a place in a country town
speaker: David
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Direct request (‘please let them give me a place’); Achish grants Ziklag in 27:6. Chapter has only the 27:11 context record.

title: Achish enlists David for war and appoints him his bodyguard
speaker: Achish
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Achish requires David to march with him (‘you will go out with me to war’) and names him chief bodyguard for life.

title: Saul asks the medium to divine and bring up Samuel
speaker: Saul
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Adds 28:8, Saul’s first request (‘divine for me… bring up the one I name’), with his oath of safety in 28:10.

title: The medium and Saul’s servants urge him to eat
speaker: the medium and Saul’s servants
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: 28:23 reports the servants joining the woman’s urging, and Saul yielding.

title: The Egyptian asks David to swear to spare him before guiding him
speaker: David; the Egyptian servant
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: David asks to be led to the raiders; the Egyptian demands an oath not to be killed or handed back to his master.

title: Abner appeals to Joab to call off the pursuit of their brothers
speaker: Abner
note: Appeal in question form (‘How long will you fail to tell the people to turn back…?’); Joab’s trumpet then recalls the army.

title: David orders Joab and the people to mourn Abner in sackcloth
speaker: David
recipient: Joab and all the people with him
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Explicit royal order: ‘Tear your garments, put on sackcloth, and beat yourselves in mourning before Abner.’

title: The people urge David to eat; he vows to fast until evening
speaker: all the people; David
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Reported urging to take the funeral meal, refused with an oath; compare ot-1-samuel-v28-22 (the medium urging Saul to eat).

title: David orders the execution of the murderers of Saul’s son
speaker: David
note: No record in this chapter. Saul’s son is called Mephibosheth in this translation (Ishbosheth in Hebrew); compare ot-2-samuel-v1-15.

title: David orders his men to strike Zion’s Jebusites with the dagger
speaker: David
note: Includes the resulting saying ‘The blind and the lame shall not enter the Lord’s house.’ Parallel 1 Chronicles 11:6 is unrecorded.

title: Toi sends his son to greet David with gifts
speaker: Toi king of Hamath
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Envoy sent with a charge to ask peace and bless David, like ot-1-samuel-v25-5. Parallel 1 Chronicles 18:10 is unrecorded.

title: David sends envoys to comfort Hanun after his father’s death
speaker: David
note: Context verse, not a flagged candidate (10:3–4 need nothing). Compare ot-1-samuel-v25-5; parallel 1 Chronicles 19:2 is unrecorded.

title: Joab arranges mutual rescue with Abishai and calls for courage
speaker: Joab
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Adds 10:11, the mutual-aid order (‘you all shall come to my rescue’). Parallel 1 Chronicles 19:12 could join ot-1-chronicles-v19-13.

title: Joab instructs the messenger how to report Uriah’s death to David
speaker: Joab
note: Detailed reported instruction (‘Then say, Your servant Uriah the Hittite also died’); no record between 11:15 and 11:25.

title: David rules that the rich man in Nathan’s parable must repay sevenfold
speaker: David
note: Royal verdict applying the restitution law (C0188, Exodus 21:37). Nathan’s commission in 12:1 is also unrecorded.

title: Amnon asks David to send Tamar to bake for him
speaker: Amnon
note: Amnon voices the request Jonadab scripted (ot-2-samuel-v13-5).

title: David sends Tamar to prepare food for Amnon
speaker: King David
note: Royal order sent to Tamar’s house: ‘Please go to the house of Amnon your brother and prepare food for him.’

title: Tamar pleads with Amnon to stop and ask the king for her
speaker: Tamar
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Adds 13:13, where her plea continues: ‘Please speak to the king now, for he certainly will not withhold me from you.’

title: Absalom invites the king and asks that Amnon attend his shearing
speaker: Absalom
note: Repeated requests (13:24, 26) and the king’s ‘Please do not let us all go’ (13:25); leads to ot-2-samuel-v13-28.

title: The Tekoite woman asks David to swear to protect her son
speaker: the woman of Tekoa
note: Her request between ot-2-samuel-v14-10 and v14-12; David answers with an oath that not a hair of her son will fall.

title: David asks the woman of Tekoa to hide nothing from him
speaker: King David
note: She then admits ‘Joab commanded me’, recalling the order already recorded at ot-2-samuel-v14-2. 14:16 needs nothing.

title: David summons Absalom and receives him with a kiss
speaker: King David
note: Reported summons ending Absalom’s exclusion (ot-2-samuel-v14-24); summonses are recorded elsewhere, e.g. ot-1-kings-v1-32.

title: Absalom asks David’s leave to go to Hebron to pay his vow
speaker: Absalom
note: The request that ot-2-samuel-v15-9 grants; a pretext for the revolt. 15:5 is narrative.

title: David asks Hushai to report palace news through the priests
speaker: David
note: Adds 15:35 (‘Whatever you hear from the king’s house, tell Zadok and Abiathar’), between the 15:34 and 15:36 records.

title: Abishai asks to behead Shimei and David forbids it
speaker: Abishai; David
note: Adds Abishai’s request, which David’s refusal answers, as AUD-10-19-22 includes Abishai’s 19:22 proposal.

title: Ahithophel advises Absalom to let him pursue David by night
speaker: Ahithophel
note: Ahithophel’s second counsel (his first is ot-2-samuel-v16-21); approved in 17:4 before Hushai is consulted.

title: Hushai counsels Absalom to muster all Israel before attacking David
speaker: Hushai the Archite
recipient: Absalom and the elders of Israel
note: Candidate 17:14 records the adoption of this counsel; 17:7–13 were not flagged as candidates and have no record.

title: Ahithophel sets his house in order before taking his life
speaker: Ahithophel
note: Reported charge (‘He gave instructions to his household’); its content is not stated.

title: Ahimaaz presses Joab, who finally tells him to run
speaker: Ahimaaz; Joab
note: Adds 18:23, completing the exchange with Joab’s permission: ‘Run.’ 18:24–28 are reports and a blessing.

title: Mephibosheth recalls ordering his servant to saddle his donkey
speaker: Mephibosheth
note: Reported order within his defence, comparable to ot-2-samuel-v1-9 (a reported request).

title: David orders Mephibosheth and Ziba to divide the land
speaker: King David
note: Royal ruling dividing Saul’s estate (compare AUD-10-9-9); Mephibosheth’s reply is ot-2-samuel-v19-31.

title: David invites Barzillai to cross over and live with him in Jerusalem
speaker: King David
note: The invitation that Barzillai declines in ot-2-samuel-v19-38.

title: David orders Amasa to summon Judah’s men within three days
speaker: King David
note: Explicit royal order; 20:5 notes Amasa’s delay, which prompts ot-2-samuel-v20-6.

title: Abel’s wise woman calls Joab near and asks him to listen
speaker: the wise woman of Abel
note: Adds 20:17: ‘Hear your handmaid’s words.’

title: Abel’s wise woman pleads with Joab to spare the city
speaker: the wise woman of Abel
note: Plea in question form (‘Why drown the Lord’s inheritance?’) citing Abel’s proverbial wisdom; Joab’s terms follow in ot-2-samuel-v20-21.

title: David longs for Bethlehem’s water, and three warriors fetch it
speaker: David
note: Indirect request (‘Who will give me water to drink?’); David pours the water out to the Lord. Parallel 1 Chronicles 11:17–19 unrecorded.

title: David appoints Benaiah to attend him and receive his orders
speaker: King David
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Reported appointment within the heroes list; parallel 1 Chronicles 11:25 is unrecorded.

title: David orders Joab to muster Israel’s tribes from Dan to Beersheba
speaker: King David
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Same census order as 1 Chronicles 21:2; distinct from the Lord’s incitement recorded at ot-2-samuel-v24-1.

title: Joab questions why David desires to count the people
speaker: Joab
note: Context verse beside candidate 24:2; the same objection recorded at 1 Chronicles 21:3.

title: The Lord tells the destroying angel to withdraw his hand
speaker: the Lord
note: ‘Enough! Now withdraw your hand’ parallels 1 Chronicles 21:15. 24:17 (prayer) and 24:19 (compliance) need nothing.

title: Nathan advises Bathsheba to remind David of his oath and promises support
speaker: Nathan the prophet
note: Adds 1:14, the last step of Nathan’s plan: he will come in after her and complete her words.

title: Bathsheba urges David to declare Solomon his successor
speaker: Bathsheba
note: Carries out ot-1-kings-v1-12; 1:20 asks the king to tell Israel who will sit on his throne.

title: Nathan asks David whether he decreed Adonijah’s succession
speaker: Nathan the prophet
note: Appeal in question form completing the plan in ot-1-kings-v1-12; compare ot-1-chronicles-v21-3. 1:21 belongs with Bathsheba’s plea.

title: Solomon spares Adonijah on condition of his good conduct
speaker: King Solomon
note: Conditional royal ruling answering ot-1-kings-v1-51, before ot-1-kings-v1-53 sends Adonijah home.

title: Dying David commands Solomon to be strong
speaker: King David
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Adds 2:1, the narrative frame of the charge: ‘he commanded his son Solomon, saying.’

title: David charges Solomon to keep the Lord’s commands in Moses’ law
speaker: King David
note: Adds 2:4, completing the sentence with God’s conditional promise: ‘If your sons guard their way, walking before Me in truth.’ 2:5 needs nothing.

title: Adonijah asks Bathsheba to request Abishag from Solomon as his wife
speaker: Adonijah
note: The request itself; ot-1-kings-v2-16 (Study Context) covers only his asking to be heard.

title: Solomon condemns Adonijah and sends Benaiah to execute him
speaker: King Solomon
note: Sworn sentence (2:24) and reported order (context verse 2:25); no record between ot-1-kings-v2-22 and v2-26.

title: Solomon reminds Shimei of his sworn confinement to Jerusalem
speaker: King Solomon
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Solomon quotes his earlier injunction and its penalty (‘you shall surely die’).

title: Solomon orders Benaiah to execute Shimei
speaker: King Solomon
note: Context verse beside candidate 2:45 (a blessing, needs nothing); the reported order ‘King Solomon commanded Benaiah’ has no record.

title: The Lord charges Solomon to keep His commandments for long life
speaker: the Lord
note: Same condition as 9:4, already linked to AUD-11-11-9; a separate Gibeon record is the alternative. 3:7–9 is prayer.

title: Hiram agrees to supply timber and asks Solomon for food
speaker: Hiram king of Tyre
note: Same exchange as 2 Chronicles 2:14; here Hiram asks food for his household and sets the raft delivery.

title: Solomon appoints Jeroboam over the forced labour of Joseph’s house
speaker: King Solomon
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Reported appointment to office; precedes Ahijah’s oracle (ot-1-kings-v11-31).

title: The Lord through Ahijah appoints Jeroboam king on condition of obedience
speaker: the Lord through Ahijah
note: ‘You shall be king over Israel… If you keep all I command you’; compare AUD-10-5-2. 11:32 and 11:35 are prediction.

title: Israel asks Rehoboam to lighten Solomon’s heavy yoke
speaker: the people of Israel
note: Parallels 2 Chronicles 10:4 and 1 Kings 12:24p, both unrecorded; Rehoboam’s reply is ot-1-kings-v12-5.

title: The elders advise Rehoboam to serve the people and speak kindly
speaker: the elders who had served Solomon
note: Counsel to a ruler, like torah-exodus-18-13 (Jethro). Parallel 2 Chronicles 10:7 unrecorded; ot-1-kings-v12-24q records only the summons.

title: The young men advise Rehoboam to answer Israel harshly
speaker: the young men raised with Rehoboam
note: Same counsel as 2 Chronicles 10:10–11; the Greek doublet 1 Kings 12:24r is also unrecorded. 12:9 is Rehoboam’s question.

title: Israel rejects David’s house and calls its men to their tents
speaker: the people of Israel
note: Same cry at 2 Samuel 20:1, 2 Chronicles 10:16 and 1 Kings 12:24t, none of them recorded.

title: Rehoboam sends Adoniram, overseer of the levy, to Israel
speaker: King Rehoboam
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Reported sending; Israel stones him. Parallel 2 Chronicles 10:18 is unrecorded.

title: Israel’s assembly summons Jeroboam and makes him king
speaker: all Israel
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Context verse beside candidate 12:21; the people’s appointment of a king has no record.

title: Rehoboam musters Judah and Benjamin to fight Israel’s house
speaker: King Rehoboam
recipient: the assembly of Judah and Benjamin
note: Parallels 2 Chronicles 11:1 and 1 Kings 12:24x, both unrecorded; countermanded by ot-1-kings-v12-23.

title: Jeroboam asks the man of God to pray for his withered hand
speaker: King Jeroboam
recipient: the man of God from Judah
note: A request to a man to intercede, like ot-1-samuel-v7-8. 13:8 (his refusal) needs nothing beyond ot-1-kings-v13-9.

title: The old prophet asks to be buried beside the man of God
speaker: the old prophet of Bethel
note: Burial instruction to his sons, comparable to ot-genesis-v47-29 (Jacob’s burial request).

title: Asa orders all Judah to carry off Ramah’s stones and timber
speaker: King Asa
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Reported royal proclamation; parallel 2 Chronicles 16:6 is also unrecorded.

title: Elijah asks the widow for water, bread and a small cake first
speaker: Elijah
note: Adds Elijah’s opening requests for water (17:10) and a morsel of bread (17:11), which lead into the cake request.

title: Elijah calls Israel to stop wavering and follow the true God
speaker: Elijah
note: ‘How long will you limp on both your knees? If the Lord is God, follow Him’; no record between 18:19 and 18:23.

title: Elijah tells Baal’s prophets to withdraw so he can offer
speaker: Elijah
note: Direction found in the Greek text (‘Move away now’); no record between ot-1-kings-v18-27 and v18-30.

summary: 52 new, 13 extend and 7 parallel findings in 65 of 138 passages, mostly unrecorded royal orders, requests and counsels in 2 Samuel and 1 Kings 1–2, 12–13 (five rest mainly on unflagged context verses).
